title: Help us build AI for Founders
intro: Eight minutes. Twenty questions and a consent line; five are optional. We are drafting a sixteen-week programme for founders whose business still runs through them, and before we decide who teaches what, we want to know whether we are teaching the right things. Your answers go to the people writing the curriculum, not to a dashboard. Version two is published with the changes marked, so you can see what moved because of you.

sections.title: Your business
sections.lead: Four quick ones so we can read the rest of your answers in context.

questions.text: Which describes you best right now?
options: Solo founder: coach, consultant, practitioner or creator. The business is me.
Founder with a team of up to ten
Founder with a team of more than ten
Planning to start a business in the next year
I lead inside someone else's company
questions.why: The one split that changes everything downstream. Solo founders and founders with a team feel the same problem differently, and every lab runs in two tracks because of it. This answer sets the wording of question 6.

questions.text: What does your business mainly sell?
questions.why: Decides which examples and skill packs we build first. A coach's company brain and an agency's company brain hold different things.

questions.text: Roughly, what is your annual revenue?
questions.why: Optional and framed as rough on purpose. In the quiz, the founders above $100K asked about data safety more than anything else; we need to know whether that holds, and at which level the finance module starts to matter.

questions.text: Which AI tools do you already use at least once a week?
options: AI built into my CRM, inbox or website tools
questions.why: Sets the floor for Get AI-Ready. If most of the room is already on one tool, the setup videos change; if many answer none yet, the onboarding layer gets longer.

sections.title: Where your hours go
sections.lead: This is the part we learn most from. The programme is measured on one number: how many hours a week the business needs you.

questions.text: In a normal week, how many hours does your business need you personally to keep running?
questions.why: The before picture. The whole programme is measured against the founder load map, and this is the first, rough reading of it across the community.

questions.text: Which of these still have to go through you? Tick everything that applies.
options: Finding leads and following them up
Deciding what to build or sell next
questions.why: The eight options are the eight modules, in plain words and in no particular order. The tick pattern tells us which pillars carry the most weight for which founder type. For solo founders the wording drops hiring and managing to delegating to contractors or AI.

questions.text: If we could take just one of those off your desk in the first month, which would it be?
questions.type: Single choice, from your answers to question 6
questions.why: Forces a priority. This is the single number that tests the module order: the draft starts with strategy, then the company brain, then marketing. If the community says sales or admin, we hear it here.

questions.text: Think of the last task you did this week that you knew AI, or someone else, should be doing. What was it, and what stopped you handing it over?
questions.why: The richest question in the survey, asked while energy is high. A story, not an opinion. The second half separates knowledge gaps from application gaps, and the words people use become lesson language.

questions.text: What has stopped you going further with AI so far? Pick up to three.
options: I do not know what to start with
I tried, and the results sounded generic or wrong
I worry about data and client confidentiality
No time to set anything up
The tools do not connect to the software I use
My team will not adopt it
I do not trust it to run without me watching
Nothing has stopped me, I am already well along
questions.why: Maps every blocker to a module: starting point to Strategy, generic output to the Company Brain, data to Module 2's governance lesson, connectors to the Get AI-Ready floor, adoption to Team, trust to the human-checkpoint design in every lab. The counts tell us where to spend lab time.

sections.title: The outline
sections.lead: Read the draft outline (the link is on this page) and tell us what you think. There are no wrong answers and nothing is fixed.

questions.text: For each of the eight modules, how much do you need it?
questions.why: A four-point need scale with no midpoint, so everyone leans one way. The share answering need it or need it urgently becomes each module's need index, by founder type.

questions.text: Which two modules would you want first?
questions.why: Order, not weight. Read together with question 7 it tells us whether the draft sequence matches how founders would choose to start.

questions.text: What problem in your business do you not see anywhere in this outline?
questions.why: The gap question, asked as a problem rather than a topic. Every answer is logged; the ones that recur become the change log in version two.

questions.text: Where should we go deeper? Name a lesson or a lab and what you would want more of.
questions.why: Depth. Tells us where a ninety-minute lab is not enough and where a module might deserve a third week.

questions.text: What would you skip or shorten?
questions.why: Permission to cut. Sixteen weeks is long; the community will tell us what they would not miss.

questions.text: Which lesson title made you think, that is me?
questions.type: Single choice, from the sixteen lesson titles
options: (The sixteen lesson titles in the outline)
questions.why: The marketing question hidden in the curriculum question. The titles that pull are the hooks for the summit and the sales page.

sections.title: How you would take part
sections.lead: Three questions on format, so the live sessions fit real lives.

questions.text: Every lab builds a system in your own business. Which works best for you?
options: Build live, in my own account, during the call
Watch the build, then do it myself afterwards with the recording
questions.why: Decides how much of each lab is guided build versus demonstration, and whether the labs need a follow-along kit.

questions.text: How will you most likely take part, and which live times could you make? Tick every time that works.
options: Live when I can, recordings otherwise
questions.why: Availability, not a promise. Attendance data from five Masteries says the hour does not move turnout; this tells us what the community can actually make and gives the final decision a second source.

questions.text: A year from now, this programme worked for you if...
questions.why: The promise, in their words. We promise hours back, every lead answered and a business designed around AI; this tells us whether that is what they are buying, and the phrases become the sales page.

sections.title: Skin in the game
sections.lead: Version two is built with the people who answer. Here is how far you want to go.

questions.text: Would you like to be part of the founding circle that shapes version two?
options: Review version two before it is published
Test one system in my own business and report back
Share my founder load map, anonymised, as an example
Be quoted, first name and business type, in the curriculum
Join a 45-minute group call with the curriculum team
Not this time, just keep me posted
questions.why: The commitment question. Everyone who ticks anything but the last option has put something in, and the list becomes the founding circle, the people most likely to enrol and most likely to tell others.

questions.text: Anything else you want the people building this to know?
questions.why: The door left open. Often the most useful answer in a survey is to the question nobody asked.

sections.title: Keeping in touch
sections.lead: Pre-filled from the email link, so this is one click.

questions.text: May we follow up with you on your answers?
questions.type: Yes or no, with email pre-filled
options: No, use my answers but do not contact me about them
questions.why: Consent, and the join to the quiz and summit records. Pre-filling the email from the campaign link removes the one field that costs completions.

thanks: Thank you. Your answers go straight to the people writing the curriculum. Version two of the outline is published on [date], with every change marked, so you can see what moved because of you. If you asked to join the founding circle you will hear from us within a week. The AI for Founders Summit runs 30 October to 1 November; your seat is saved at [link].
design_notes: Length: about eight minutes. Twenty questions plus the consent line; five are optional (revenue, and four of the open questions). Everything optional is marked so.
Order: easy facts first (1 to 4), then the big open question (8) while energy is high, the outline grid in the middle, commitment at the end. The contact question is last and pre-filled.
One idea per question. No double-barrelled questions, no leading wording, no agree/disagree statements. Scales have four points and no midpoint, so everyone leans one way.
Open questions ask for a story or a specific, never an opinion: the last task you did this week, name a lesson, a year from now. Specifics are quotable; opinions are not.
Branching: question 1 sets the wording of question 6 (solo founders see delegating to contractors or AI in place of hiring and managing). Question 7 lists only what was ticked in 6.
The outline is linked from the survey and shown inline before question 10, so nobody has to leave the form to answer.
Incentive is recognition, not a prize: early sight of version two, a named place in the thank-you section, the founding circle. Warm leads respond to being taken seriously.
Send on a Tuesday, remind on Friday, close the following Tuesday. One reminder only, to non-openers and partial completions.
Mobile first, progress shown, email pre-filled from the campaign link. Typeform or an Airtable form; responses land in the AI for Founders base once Vishen has aligned, in a sheet until then.
analysis: Segment every answer by founder type (question 1) and revenue band (question 3). The draft already runs two tracks; this tells us whether two is enough.
Module need index: the share answering need it or need it urgently on question 10, by segment. Read against questions 7 and 11 to test the module order.
Blocker map: question 9 counts against the module each blocker maps to. Where a blocker is common and its module is late in the programme, we move the fix earlier or into Get AI-Ready.
Language mining: questions 8, 12 and 18 are read in full, not summarised. Recurring phrases become lesson language and sales-page copy; recurring problems become the version two change log.
Format: questions 16 and 17 set lab design and give the time-slot decision a second source alongside the attendance data.
Founding circle: everyone who ticks an active option in question 19 goes on a list with their answers attached. They see version two first.
Version two is published with a change log that credits the survey: what moved, and roughly how many people asked for it.
